luca: Quick recap — I finished a set of KV prefix-cache benchmarks using the replay harness against staging (redwood-13b-serve-v2). Goal was apples-to-apples vs synthetic traffic and to exercise warmup, eviction, and concurrency correctness. Ran a replay of ~1.8M sampled prod requests (2025-11..2026-02). Concurrency sweep: 64,128,256,512,1024. Warmup: 60s; steady-state: 10m. Key findings below.

luca: Findings: 
- Prefix cache hit-rate converges ~78% at concurrency <=256, drops to ~62% at 1024 due to eviction storms.
- Warmup time to 70% hit-rate: ~45s at 128, ~120s at 1024.
- Evictions are bursty: observed 4 eviction spikes per run when concurrent writes exceed per-shard threshold.
- Correctness: found 2 rare instances of stale KV reads under heavy concurrent prefix-merges (repro rate ~0.002%).
- Performance: p50 token latency unchanged on hits (~7.2ms), p95 increases on miss-heavy scenarios from 142ms -> 155ms (≈9% regression) compared against a synthetic baseline run.

luca: Repro command used for the main run (harness):
```
./replay_harness --trace samples/prod_trace_202602.jsonl \
  --model redwood-13b-serve-v2 --concurrency 512 \
  --warmup 60s --duration 10m --seed 42 \
  --kv-cache-enabled --prefix-caching=on --batcher-config configs/batcher/steady.json
```

anya: Nice. Did you keep batcher config, quantization, and kernel selection identical between the synthetic and replay runs? We need those to claim apples-to-apples.

luca: Yes — everything pinned: same model binary, same quant (int8-qat), same kernel-selection map. The only variable is request distribution (synthetic uniform vs real trace distribution). I also ran a control where we fed the replay but randomized prefixes to check sensitivity — hit-rate dropped by ~18% which matches expectations.

mike: Numbers snapshot from last run (concurrency sweep):
- 64: hit 80.4%, p50 7.1ms, p95 138ms
- 128: hit 79.1%, p50 7.1ms, p95 140ms
- 256: hit 77.8%, p50 7.2ms, p95 143ms
- 512: hit 72.3%, p50 7.3ms, p95 148ms
- 1024: hit 62.0%, p50 7.6ms, p95 155ms and a burst of evictions causing ~5s window of elevated miss-rate

mike: Note: measured KV cache effectiveness as (cache_hits / cache_lookups) aggregated at 1s buckets; prefix merges are heavy for some customers and dominate write rate.

chen: On the correctness issue — I dug into the trace for one repro sample. We saw a prefix merge + concurrent read where the reader observed a partially applied merged entry because eviction and merge logic used separate non-atomic steps. Pseudo repro: 
```
// simplified
if (!cache.contains(k)) insert_partial(k, v_part1);
merge_remaining(k, v_part2); // not atomic with readers
```
Result: reader sees v_part1 and treats as complete.

chen: Fix suggestion: make merge an atomic swap (build new merged blob off-thread, then single atomic pointer swap). Alternatively, per-key lightweight lock or use per-shard version counters that readers validate. I implemented a small PoC atomic-swap in local run — repro rate dropped to 0.

anya: Good catch. For the eviction storms — is it per-shard LRU kicking in because of skewed hot prefixes? Can we adjust shard-count or eviction batch size?

luca: Yes, spikes align with hot-prefix churn; current eviction strategy is per-shard LRU with batch-evict when >75% full. At high concurrency many shards hit threshold simultaneously. Ideas: 
- stagger eviction windows across shards (randomized backoff)
- increase eviction batch size to reduce churn frequency (but each eviction is expensive)
- adaptive per-shard watermarks based on recent miss-rate

mike: I ran a quick comparison of staggered backoff vs immediate batch-evict: backoff reduced simultaneous eviction events by ~85% and smoothed hit-rate drops, p95 improved by ~6% in the 512/1024 runs. Will push results to the perf dashboard.

perf-bot: perf-bot: auto-detected perf delta on staging for redwood-13b-serve-v2: p95 token latency +9% (miss-heavy 1024 run) — linked flamegraphs and traces at https://perf.internal/reports/1719123456. Tagging #perf #kv-cache.

luca: Action items: 
- I will open INFR-2311 with full repro (trace + harness config + flamegraphs).
- chen to prep atomic-merge patch + unit tests for concurrent reads.
- mike to formalize staggered-evict config and run A/B vs baseline.
- anya to coordinate QA: run deterministic replay with a smaller sample set to validate fix doesn't regress throughput.

luca: TL;DR: prefix caching shows strong wins at normal concurrency but suffers eviction storms and rare concurrency correctness issues. Short-term mitigations (staggered eviction + atomic merges) look promising; next is an apples-to-apples A/B on staging before rolling to dedicated infra. :thumbsup:
